\subtitle{Relational Validity Checks for Learning-Assisted\\
Satellite Communication Experiments\\[0.9em]

% ============================================================ 2. motivation
\begin{frame}{Ordering alone is not deployment validity}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      Learning components now sit inside satellite communication software ---
      correcting a propagated orbit, adapting a link parameter, gating a learned branch.

      \vspace{0.9em}
      These systems are temporal, so we evaluate with a chronological split.
      That is \emph{necessary}, and well established.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{The claim of this paper}
        It is \alert{not sufficient} --- and the gap is one of \emph{kind}, not degree.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.4em}
      \small A passing split can coexist with a deployment claim that was never checkable
      from the data in hand.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Train on the past, test on the future --- and still not be able to say the
       experiment was valid.}
\end{frame}

       or a second aggregation level.}

% ============================================================ 5. method overview
\begin{frame}{Orbit-Evidence: validity as an executable contract}
  \vspace{-0.4em}
  \begin{center}\input{figures/fig_arch.tex}\end{center}
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \only<1>{\msgflush{The experiment acts at $t_d$ from state it already holds.}}
  \only<2>{\msgflush{A \texttt{numpy}-only checker, run like a test suite: \Nrules{} rules in four layers.}}
  \only<3>{\msgflush{Two cannot: the relational checks compare executions, or aggregation levels.}}
  \only<4>{\msgflush{A design that cannot support a decision returns \textsc{indeterminate} --- never \textsc{pass}.}}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 6. two key ideas
\begin{frame}{The two relational checks}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{L4.6 --- differential provenance}
        Two runs, same \emph{manifest} --- the record of everything a run declared it
        depended on --- but \alert{different output} $\Rightarrow$ the record is incomplete.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.3em}
      \small
      Refutes a claim of completeness \emph{without enumerating} the dependencies a manifest
      might omit. One-sided by construction: failure is evidence, success is not certification.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{L4.7 --- statistical-unit adequacy}
        Does dependence survive \alert{one declared level coarser}?
        Null: shuffling the group labels changes nothing.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.3em}
      \small
      And it \emph{abstains}. With too few groups, the smallest $p$ the test can
      \emph{possibly} produce already exceeds $\alpha$ --- that design could not have rejected at
      any effect size. Not weak evidence: no evidence either way. It returns
      \textsc{indeterminate}.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{One judgement generates both: neither obligation can be certified,
       so we accept checks that can only \emph{refuse}.}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 8. real satellite evidence
% H3: the cohort and the primary in-track analysis have DIFFERENT denominators. The first
% version stacked 331 / 109 / 11 next to rho-hat = 0.501 and so implied all 331 passes entered
% the ICC. They did not: 59 have no successor element set, leaving 272 in 90 element sets.
\begin{frame}{Does the unit problem appear in real orbital data?}
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      \centering
      \begin{tikzpicture}[x=1mm,y=1mm,font=\scriptsize,
        c/.style={draw=black!45,line width=0.5pt,fill=black!3,align=center,inner sep=1mm,
                  text width=44mm,minimum height=6mm},
        a/.style={draw=black!60,line width=0.7pt,fill=blue!6,align=center,inner sep=1mm,
                  text width=44mm,minimum height=6mm},
        h/.style={font=\scriptsize\bfseries,text=black!70,anchor=west}]
        \node[h] at (0,27) {source cohort};
        \node[c] at (20,21) {\Npasses{} predicted visible passes};
        \node[c] at (20,14) {\Nelsets{} element sets (orbit solutions)};
        \node[c] at (20, 7) {\Nobjects{} objects};
        \draw[->,line width=0.7pt,black!60] (20,2.8) -- (20,-1.5);
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=black!55,anchor=north,align=center] at (20,-3.0)
          {$-\Natdropped$ passes: no later orbit solution to compare};
        \node[h] at (0,-11) {primary in-track analysis};
        \node[a] at (20,-17) {\Natused{} passes};
        \node[a] at (20,-24) {from \Natgroups{} element sets that have a later one};
      \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \small\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2pt}
      \begin{tabular}{@{}l l@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{grouping} & \textbf{verdict}\\
        \midrule
        pass $\to$ element set & $\hat{\rho}=\Naticc$\\
        \Natused{} in \Natgroups{} & $p=\Natp$\\
                                   & lower bound $\Natlo$\\
                                   & \textbf{HALT}\\
        \addlinespace
        element set $\to$ object & $\hat{\rho}=\Naticcelset$\\
        \Natelsetunits{} in \Natelsetgroups{} & \textbf{HALT}\\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{0.4em}
      {\scriptsize Both $p$ at $1/400$ --- the floor of a 400-permutation test. Measured: how far
      an orbit solution moves \emph{along its own track} when the next one replaces it ---
      \textbf{not truth error}. On a purely \emph{geometric} quantity the same rule returned
      $\hat{\rho}=\Nrealiccab$: the observable decides.}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

        \node[h] at (20,26) {original};
        \node[h] at (48,26) {corrected};
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=black!70,anchor=east] at (10,18) {overlap};
        \node[o] at (24,18) {\Nconsoverlap\% of val.\ support};
        \node[c] at (52,18) {\Nconsoverlapcorr{}};
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=black!70,anchor=east] at (10,9) {\rulename{L4.1}};
        \node[o] at (24,9) {HALT};
        \node[c] at (52,9) {PASS};
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=black!70,anchor=east] at (10,0) {checkpoint};

        \draw[->,line width=0.7pt,black!55] (36,9) -- (40,9);

      \vspace{0.6em}
      {\scriptsize Re-running one seed reproduces its checkpoint \textbf{bit for bit} ---
      the intervention, not training noise.}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.42\textwidth}
      \small The \emph{third-party model's} detection metric moved on three seeds, \emph{in both directions}.

      \vspace{0.5em}
      Not a null: at \Nconsseeds{} paired seeds the smallest attainable two-sided $p$ is
      $\Nconsminp > \alpha$.

      \vspace{0.5em}
      $\Rightarrow$ \textbf{not estimable} at the available paired-run resolution --- an
      evidentiary limit of \emph{this study}, not a rule verdict and not a null result.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Model selection changed; the downstream endpoint is not estimable at this resolution.}

% ============================================================ 10. what is new
\begin{frame}{What is actually new}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{Not the primitives.}\\[0.3em]
      \small ICC(1), permutation inference, metamorphic relations, hermetic build closure,
      mutation testing --- all established, none proposed here.\normalsize

      \vspace{0.6em}
      \textbf{Not a checklist.}\\[0.3em]
      \small The \Nrules{} rules are the satellite \emph{instantiation}, not the
      contribution.\normalsize
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{The method is the conversion}
        {\small
        \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.25em}
          \item Identify which validity obligations are \emph{relational}.
          \item Choose the counterfactual execution or coarser level that makes each
                \emph{falsifiable}.
          \item Encode the invariant as a contract --- and let an undecidable case return
                \textsc{indeterminate} rather than pass.
        \end{enumerate}}
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.2em}
      {\small A permutation reference is ordinarily an analysis step. Here it calibrates a
      \emph{gate} --- with an operating characteristic and an abstention state.}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Change what is tested, not how much.}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 11. limitations
\begin{frame}{What this does not establish}
  \vspace{0.2em}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      {\small
      \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.5em}
        \item \textbf{No completeness claim.} L4.6 is bounded by the caller's variation set;
              the input nobody thought of is absent by construction.
        \item \textbf{No RF or packet-level result.} The object of study is the experiment,
              not the link.
        \item \textbf{No improvement in learned accuracy.} The contract refuses claims;
              it does not make models better.
      \end{itemize}}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      {\small
      \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.5em}
        \item \textbf{Represented-fault regression coverage only.} Faults and rules largely
              share an origin, so curated coverage measures \emph{reachability}, not
              fault-finding power.
        \item \textbf{One outside dataset, one outside model.} One step away from marking
              our own homework --- not zero.
        \item \textbf{PASS means not rejected}, never verified.
      \end{itemize}}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{A validity method must apply the same evidence discipline to its own claims.}
\end{frame}

  and allowed to \textbf{refuse} an unsupported claim.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- why the abstention floor is not a power floor}
  % NOT {\small ...}: beamer reads a brace group at the start of a frame body as the SUBTITLE
  % argument, so the whole slide silently vanished. Set the size without a group.
  \small
  Take the specific construction of \emph{three coarser groups of two units}: it admits
  $6!/(2!^{3}3!) = 15$ distinct assignments, so the smallest attainable $p$ is
  $1/15 = 0.067 > \alpha$. That design cannot reject at the nominal level at any effect size.

  \vspace{0.5em}
  \emph{Four} groups of two admit $105$ assignments, whose exhaustive reference reaches $0.0095$.
  The general rule is stated at the rule level, not by extrapolating $1/15$: designs below the
  registered resolution floor return \textsc{indeterminate}.

  \vspace{0.8em}
  So \textsc{indeterminate} is a statement about the \emph{design's resolution}, not about the
  strength of the effect. Collapsing it into \textsc{pass} is how a design that could not have
  rejected comes to look like one that did not.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- reproduction and provenance}
  \small
  \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.4em}
    \item \texttt{make gate} regenerates the fault matrix and L4.7's operating characteristic,
          and \emph{refuses to build} if a headline number disagrees with the artifact at the
          sentence claiming it. The manuscript contains \Nclaimsites{} artifact-bound claim
          sites; every numerical value shown in this deck is generated from that same summary
          artifact.
    \item The two external studies are hash-matched rather than regenerated: their inputs do
          not ship.
    \item \texttt{make external-consequence-verify} checks the committed third-party results
          against the frozen commit, the frozen detector hash and the recorded data hashes ---
          16 checks, no training.
    \item The telemetry arrays came from a \emph{checksum-verified mirror} after the upstream
          endpoint became unavailable; per-file hashes matched two independently published
          checksum sources. That is mirror concordance, \emph{not} verification by the original
          publisher.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
